eot_semantics.definition: EOT (tokenizer id 200) is the completion terminator: record_ids supervises `code + \n + EOT` so EOT is a trained completion target exactly once per record and generation stops on it via model.generate/trajectory_generate
eot_semantics.exploratory_decoding_policy: eot_gated trajectory_generate masks EOT only while the completion sits inside an open construct (inference policy, NOT a model change)

experiment.hardware: CPU-only host (5 cores, 5.92 GB RAM, 0 CUDA devices)
experiment.pre_registered_hypothesis: EOT self-emission inside open constructs is a consequence of the 49.84% mid-construct training windows, not of a decoding defect; EOT is the trained completion terminator (supervised exactly once per record as the final completion target)
experiment.acceptance_criteria: EOT semantics documented, not redefined; eot-gated decoding is an EXPLORATORY inference-time policy and never evidence of model learning; fixed decoding stays primary
